question: Does the 2023 fish-microplastics paper provide Marikina-specific species evidence that can be safely reconciled despite a conflicting repository withdrawal label?
citation: Espiritu, E. Q., Rodolfo, R. S., Evangelista, S. M. J., Feliciano, J. J. G., Sumaway, A. M. N., Pauco, J. L. R., Alvarez, K. V. N., & Enriquez, E. P. (2023). Microplastics contamination in the fishes of selected sites in Pasig River and Marikina River in the Philippines. Marine Pollution Bulletin, 187, 114573. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.marpolbul.2023.114573

sourceAccess.accessMethod: Reviewed the PubMed bibliographic record and abstract, Ateneo Research Portal publication metadata, both duplicate Ateneo Archium records, and the indexed Elsevier publisher abstract/highlights on 2026-11-19. Direct publisher-page retrieval returned HTTP 403, so no full article was accessed or retained. A PubMed E-utilities XML check found no CommentsCorrectionsList entry for this PMID. A bounded exact-title/DOI search did not identify a separate publisher withdrawal or retraction notice; this is not proof that none exists.
sourceAccess.articleStatusConflict: PubMed and the Ateneo Research Portal classify the article as a journal article published in February 2023. Archium record /112/ carries the citation and abstract without a withdrawal label, while duplicate record /115/ ends with 'This paper has been withdrawn.' The repository pages do not explain the duplicate or the scope/date of that notice. Do not treat this conflicting repository label alone as a verified formal article retraction or dismissal.
sourceAccess.boundedNoticeSearchLimit: The searches covered the exact DOI/title and the reviewed PubMed metadata as of 2026-11-19; publication status remains unresolved until an authoritative clarification is available.
sourceAccess.licenseFinding: PubMed and the Ateneo Research Portal state publisher copyright © 2023 Elsevier Ltd. All rights reserved. No item-specific open reuse license was identified. Only bibliographic metadata and concise findings are recorded; no abstract text, article text, table, image, or raw publisher content is reproduced.

abstractFindings.publicationDate: Published February 2023; the accessible abstract does not state collection dates.
abstractFindings.methodAsReported: Raman microspectroscopy for microplastic imaging and identification.
abstractFindings.publisherHighlightAsIndexed: Janitor fish from Marikina River had the most number of ingested microplastics.
abstractFindings.siteAndTaxonResolution: The abstract lists the three scientific taxa across selected sites along both rivers but does not allocate each taxon to a particular river or station. The publisher highlight identifies a Marikina janitor-fish group but does not give its scientific name. Although Pterygoplichthys is often called janitor fish, the accessible article metadata does not explicitly crosswalk this highlight to Pterygoplichthys spp.; do not make that assignment from common-name convention alone.
abstractFindings.relatedExistingEvidence: The repository already contains a separate 2011 Marikina Pterygoplichthys barcode review and a four-site 2021–2022 fish-host cohort review. This paper does not resolve the 2011 station/voucher assignment questions and is not treated as independent confirmation of a species-level Marikina occurrence.

evidenceDecision.decision: Retain as a research-only publication and contamination-context lead; do not use it to add a species or occurrence row until the publisher-status conflict and scientific-name-to-river link are independently resolved.
evidenceDecision.reason: The article metadata is inconsistent across duplicate repository records; the full article was inaccessible; and the accessible abstract/highlights do not explicitly link a scientific taxon to the Marikina samples. This study concerns microplastics, not fish presence, catchability, diet, or a current water-safety determination.

nonClaims: The Archium /115/ withdrawn label is not independently verified as a formal publisher retraction or as applying to the DOI-level article record.
Oreochromis niloticus, Arius manillensis, and Pterygoplichthys spp. are listed for the combined two-river study; the abstract does not establish which taxon was sampled from Marikina River.
The indexed Marikina janitor-fish highlight does not supply an explicit scientific-name crosswalk, voucher, station, collection date, or count in the accessible content.
This paper does not establish current presence, abundance, catchability, legal harvest, fishing access, diet guidance, or whether fish or river water are safe to consume or use.
The paper is not counted as an independent corroborating survey for the previously reviewed Marikina Pterygoplichthys material.
nextActions: If a lawful full-text copy becomes available, verify publication/withdrawal status from the publisher and inspect the methods, sample table, and explicit site-by-taxon assignments before changing any evidence disposition.
Keep fish-contamination findings separate from species-occurrence, food-safety, and water-safety datasets; do not project the abstract's general health-risk wording as local advice.
Continue the NCR freshwater, brackish, marine, and waterbody-scope review; NCR and Luzon remain incomplete.
